## Problem

Work items with 'in-progress' status are not appearing blue in the TUI tree view, despite having the correct status. This affects WL-0ML16W7000D2M8J3 and other in-progress items.

## Root Cause

The titleColorForStatus() function in src/commands/helpers.ts uses chalk to generate ANSI color codes, but blessed's list component doesn't properly interpret ANSI codes in text strings. Blessed expects its own markup tags (e.g. {cyan-fg}text{/cyan-fg}) instead.

When colored text with ANSI codes is passed to blessed, the codes are lost or misinterpreted, causing the TUI list to not display the correct colors.

## Solution

Replace chalk color codes with blessed markup tags in the titleColorForStatus() and renderTitle() functions. This allows blessed's built-in tag parser (tags: true is already enabled on the list component) to properly render the colors.

The mapping should be:
- 'in-progress' → {cyan-fg}text{/cyan-fg} (was chalk.cyan)
- 'completed' → {gray-fg}text{/gray-fg} (was chalk.gray)
- 'blocked' → {red-fg}text{/red-fg} (was chalk.redBright)
- 'open' (default) → {green-fg}text{/green-fg} (was chalk.greenBright)

Note: This change only affects TUI output. Other uses of chalk in helpers.ts (console output, conflict resolution display) should remain unchanged since those aren't going to blessed.

## Related Files

- src/commands/helpers.ts - titleColorForStatus() and renderTitle() functions (lines 61-80)
- src/commands/tui.ts - uses formatTitleOnly() to render tree items (line 949)
- src/tui/components/list.ts - blessed list component with tags: true enabled (line 24)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Work items with 'in-progress' status appear cyan/blue in the TUI tree view
2. Work items with 'completed' status appear gray in the TUI tree view
3. Work items with 'blocked' status appear red in the TUI tree view
4. Work items with 'open' status appear green in the TUI tree view (or other default color)
5. WL-0ML16W7000D2M8J3 now appears blue in the tree
6. All existing tests pass
7. No changes to console output formatting (chalk usage outside TUI remains unchanged)
data.title: Fix TUI work item colors: use blessed markup instead of chalk ANSI codes

data.description:
Problem statement
The Worklog CLI lacks a dependency management command, preventing users from recording and inspecting dependency edges via the CLI. This intake defines a minimal `wl dep` command set and outputs to enable dependency tracking workflows without edge types.

Users
- Developers and agents managing work items who need to declare and view dependencies from the CLI.
- Maintainers who need a human-readable and JSON output for automation.

User stories
- As a developer, I want to add a dependency so I can track what blocks a work item.
- As a maintainer, I want to list both inbound and outbound dependencies so I can see what is blocked and what is blocking.
- As an automation user, I want JSON output with key fields to parse dependencies programmatically.

Success criteria
- `wl dep add <item> <depends-on>` creates a dependency edge where item depends on depends-on.
- `wl dep rm <item> <depends-on>` removes the dependency edge if present.
- `wl dep list <item>` shows two sections: “Depends on” and “Depended on by”, even when empty.
- Human output lists ids, titles, status, priority, and direction; JSON includes the same fields.
- Missing ids produce warnings and the command exits 0.

Constraints
- No dependency types or type validation.
- Minimal CLI surface (add/rm/list only) with existing global flags support (e.g., --json).
- Non-destructive behavior for missing ids (warn and continue).

Existing state
- Worklog has blocked status handling and parses blocking ids from descriptions/comments.
- No `wl dep` CLI exists in `CLI.md`, and no dependency edge storage is implemented in code.

Desired change
- Implement `wl dep add|rm|list` commands for dependency edges without types.
- Ensure list output includes inbound and outbound sections with detailed fields.
- Add warnings for missing ids without failing the command.

Related work
- WL-0ML2VPUOT1IMU5US — Add wl dep command (this intake)
- WL-0ML4PH4EQ1XODFM0 — Doctor: detect missing dep references (child item)
- WL-0MKRPG64S04PL1A6 — Feature: worklog doctor (integrity checks)
- `CLI.md` — CLI reference, currently missing dep command

Suggested next step
- Proceed to the five review passes for this intake draft, then update WL-0ML2VPUOT1IMU5US with the approved brief.
data.title: Add wl dep command

Summary: Extend wl dep list to support directional filtering for dependency edges.

User story:
- As an agent, I want to query only outbound dependencies for a work item so I can check whether a dependency edge already exists without client-side filtering.

Expected behavior:
- wl dep list <itemId> --outgoing --json returns only outbound edges (item depends on dependsOn).
- wl dep list <itemId> --incoming --json returns only inbound edges (items that depend on item).
- If neither flag is provided, retain current behavior (both directions).
- If both flags are provided, return an error (preferred behavior).
- JSON output shape unchanged aside from filtered contents.

Acceptance criteria:
- CLI help documents --outgoing and --incoming for wl dep list.
- Filtering works in both human and --json output.
- Unit tests cover outbound-only, inbound-only, and default behavior.
- Backward compatibility: existing usage without flags continues to work.

Notes:
- Ensure error messaging is clear when both flags are provided.

User story:
- As an agent, I want to use --body when adding comments so CLI usage is consistent with other systems and less error-prone.

- wl comment add <workItemId> --body "text" behaves exactly like --comment "text".
- If both --body and --comment are provided, return a clear validation error.
- Help text documents --body as an alias for --comment.

Acceptance criteria:
- Alias works for wl comment add and wl comment create.
- Help output lists --body in both commands.
- Unit tests cover alias use and conflict error.
- Backward compatibility: --comment continues to work unchanged.

data.description:
Summary: Add a new dialog option and keybinding in the TUI Next Item dialog to advance to the next recommended item (next-next).

User story:
- As a user, I want to skip a recommended item in the Next Item dialog so I can move to subsequent recommendations when the first is blocked.

Expected behavior:
- The Next Item dialog includes an option (e.g., 'Next recommendation') that advances to the next recommended work item.
- Pressing 'n' while the Next Item dialog is open triggers the same behavior.
- Each activation advances the dialog to show the next recommendation (second, third, etc.).
- Existing options (e.g., view selected item, cancel) continue to work.
- If there is no further recommendation, show a clear message and keep the dialog open.

Acceptance criteria:
- New dialog option present and labeled clearly.
- 'n' keybinding works while the Next Item dialog is open.
- Dialog updates to show the next recommended item on each use.
- Behavior is covered by unit or integration tests.
- Backward compatibility: existing dialog behavior unchanged when not using the new option.
data.title: Add next-next option to Next Item dialog

Summary:
Add two optional CLI flags to work item create/update commands to control ordering:  and .

User stories:
- As a user I can set an explicit numeric ordering when creating or updating a work item using  so items appear in a predictable position.
- As a user I can insert a new or updated item after an existing sibling using , which computes a  between the referenced item and its next sibling.

Expected behaviour:
- Both flags are optional; omit both and current behaviour is unchanged.
-  accepts a validated integer and sets the work item's  to that value.
-  resolves the referenced work item to its numeric , then computes a new  as the midpoint between that value and the next sibling's  (or a defined max/default if no next sibling).
- Resolve  to a numeric  before creating/updating to ensure atomic update and avoid races.
- If  is provided together with ,  takes precedence and  is ignored.

Implementation notes:
- Validate integer input for  at CLI parsing layer; reject non-integers with a clear error.
- : Accepts a work item id; resolve to numeric  server-side (or via an atomic server call) before creating/updating the new item to avoid races.
- When computing midpoint, use a numeric scheme that maintains precision and avoids collisions on concurrent inserts (e.g., use large integer space or rationals; consider fallback rebalancing when no midpoint available).
- Add unit tests for CLI parsing and sort index calculation and integration tests that simulate concurrent inserts.
- Backwards-compatible: both flags optional; no change to existing behaviour when omitted.

Acceptance criteria (testable):
1) CLI accepts  as integer; creating/updating an item with this flag sets  to the provided value.
2) CLI accepts ; creating an item with this flag places it after the referenced sibling by computing an appropriate .
3) When both flags are omitted, behaviour unchanged.
4) Input validation tests for invalid integers and non-existent  ids return user-friendly errors.
5) Concurrency integration test: two concurrent inserts using  against the same predecessor produce distinct orderings and remain stable.

Tests to add:
- Unit tests: CLI parser accepts flags and validates types;  midpoint calculation returns expected numeric values and handles edge cases.
- Integration tests: simulate concurrent creation with  to assert no collisions and acceptable ordering.

Backwards compatibility: both flags are optional and do not change current APIs when omitted.

data.author: OpenCode
data.comment:
Fixed textarea viewport/scrolling issue when using Ctrl+Enter

Problem: When pressing Ctrl+Enter to add a new line, the first line would disappear and only reappear when typing a character.

Root cause: The textarea was setting the new value before the dialog had expanded, causing rendering issues with the viewport.

Solution in commit cdf5991:
- Update layout and expand dialog BEFORE setting the new value
- Improved scroll calculation to properly keep cursor line visible
- Added viewport handling when box height changes
- Force internal cursor update to refresh the display

The textarea now properly displays all content when adding new lines.

data.author: OpenCode
data.comment:
FOUND THE ROOT CAUSE! Fixed textarea scroll issue in commit abe7e24

Problem: When pressing Ctrl+Enter to add lines, the first line would disappear.

Root Cause: The textarea has scrollable=true and maintains internal scroll state. When adding a newline:
1. The cursor moves to line 2
2. The dialog expands to fit 2 lines
3. But the textarea's scroll position wasn't being reset
4. If scroll was > 0, line 1 would be scrolled off the top

Solution: Explicitly set scroll to 0 whenever totalLines <= visibleLines. This ensures all content is visible from the top when it fits in the viewport.

The fix was simple - we were only setting scroll when content EXCEEDED the visible area, but never resetting it to 0 when content should be fully visible.

data.author: OpenCode
data.comment:
SUCCESS! Fixed the Ctrl+Enter textarea rendering issue in commit ae5b9e2

The root cause was finally identified:
1. Ctrl+Enter sends a 'linefeed' keypress event (not 'C-enter')
2. Blessed's textarea handles this internally and inserts the newline
3. Our .key(['C-enter']) handler never ran because blessed processed it first
4. We were resizing AFTER the newline was inserted, causing scroll issues

The solution:
- Intercept the 'linefeed' keypress event BEFORE blessed processes it
- Read the current line count
- Calculate the future line count (current + 1)
- Resize the dialog preemptively to the correct height
- Let blessed insert the newline naturally
- Scroll to bottom after insertion completes

Now when pressing Ctrl+Enter:
- The box expands smoothly
- All content remains visible
- The cursor stays visible on the new line
- No content scrolls off screen unexpectedly

This was a complex debugging journey that involved understanding blessed's internal event handling!

data.author: @AGENT
data.comment:
Plan to fix overwrite (single-machine, concurrent writers):

Root cause: multiple WorklogDatabase instances hold stale snapshots. Any write exports the instance snapshot to JSONL, so a stale instance can overwrite newer changes from another instance.

Recommended fix (Option 1): merge-on-export in WorklogDatabase.exportToJsonl.
- Before writing JSONL, load current JSONL from disk and merge with in-memory snapshot using mergeWorkItems/mergeComments (newer updatedAt wins; non-default beats default).
- Write merged result back to JSONL.
Why it works: prevents stale writers from overwriting newer fields; each write reconciles with latest on-disk state.

Alternatives:
- Import-before-write guard based on JSONL mtime (simpler but still racey).
- File lock around JSONL writes (robust but more complexity).

Plan:
1) Implement merge-on-export in WorklogDatabase.exportToJsonl.
2) Update failing regression test in tests/sync.test.ts to pass.
3) Run npm test -- --run tests/sync.test.ts.

Expected outcome: stale snapshot imports no longer revert recent updates.
